entities.name: PMID:25086705
observations: 2014 Environmental Research study of extreme temperature and diabetes mortality in urban Harbin and Chongqing, China.
Used a double-threshold B-spline distributed lag non-linear model over lags 0–30 days, controlling for potential confounders including air pollutants.

entities.name: Diabetes mellitus
observations: The study assessed mortality attributed to diabetes mellitus in metropolitan areas of Harbin and Chongqing.

entities.name: Extreme temperature diabetes mortality
observations: Both extreme cold and extreme heat were significantly associated with diabetes mortality in Harbin and Chongqing, with location-specific lag structures.
Harbin: cold peak RR 1.223 (95% CI 1.054–1.418) at −23 °C, lag 5; heat peak RR 1.343 (95% CI 1.080–1.670) at 37 °C, lag 2.
Chongqing: cold peak RR 1.201 (95% CI 1.006–1.434) at 4 °C, lag 7; heat peak RR 1.811 (95% CI 1.083–3.027) at 41 °C, lag 0.
Unit risks per 1 °C change: Harbin cold 12.9% (95% CI 2.5–33.7%), heat 16.5% (3.8–39.1%); Chongqing cold 12.5% (−4.7–47.5%), heat 19.7% (3.9–48.5%).
